With the start of UNGA, electrification is moving to the centre of the development agenda. 

Are we able to move from ambition to implementation?


“35 by 35” captures the scale of the challenge: increasing electricity’s share of global final energy consumption from just over 20% today to 35% by 2035.

Tomorrow, at #UNGA81, on September 22, the COP31 Presidency, the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the United Nations will convene the third High-Level Energy Transitions Solutions Dialogue during UNGA High-Level Week.

The discussion will focus on the systems needed to support electrification across transport, buildings and industry, including stronger grids, storage and flexibility:

* Global grid investment is expected to reach around US$550 billion in 2026, up 17% in one year, although higher equipment costs account for part of this growth.
* Battery storage investment is expected to exceed US$100 billion.
* More than 2,500 GW of renewable generation, storage and large-load projects are waiting in grid connection queues worldwide.

The dialogue will also address energy efficiency, clean cooking and energy security, with a focus on moving these priorities into national plans, investment pipelines and implementation.

UNDP is supporting countries to translate global energy ambitions into country-level delivery and impact at scale.

I look forward to the discussion around advancing the systems, financing and partnerships required to deliver 35 by 35.
